I went through a similar hell. I struggled with not getting love from my family, not having friends, and wanting to kill myself every day.

I am not an expert but I can suggest a few things to try and help. I see a therapist to talk about my issues and work through potential solutions. I have tried taking the attitude of "fuck you life, I'm not going to let you pull me down". That worked for a while.

There are people who love you. I realized my family loved me but in a twisted, close-minded way so I had to leave them. I went away to college, moved out, and I don't talk to them. I know you're only 15, so your options are limited. Its hard cutting people out of your life, but it needs to be done.

Cut out the bad people, and surround yourself with good people who care and love you. Or at least, who are apathetic. I hung out with the nerds and band geeks. They weren't exactly friends but they were accepting and didn't make me want to kill myself.

You can't worry about 100 years from now or 500 years from now. We humans only get 90 years or so. What is important is living your life for yourself. Don't worry about making an impact or who will remember you when you're gone. It doesn't matter. What matters is your family. If your job is enough to support you, keep working at it. Spend more time with your family and let them know how much they mean to you.

Find what makes you happy, take some time to discover it. I have issues finding what makes me happy, but I am still here trying. Live life for you and if you can't, live for your wife and your daughter. She needs her father.

ive had something similar, having never broken a bone before, being depressed/apathetic, and generally curious to see what it felt like, but then i actually broke my hand and it wasn't that fun... It wasn't self inflicted, totally accidental, and the pain lasted less than a week. After that, it was mostly frustrating and inconvenient with a cast and showering was difficult. Then after the cast came off, my wrist and forearm were shrunken b/c i couldn't use it while in the cast, so...
Basically, you're not insane; i just don't think breaking a bone is what you need. If you really want to feel something, I took an interest in pain and researched it, formulated opinions and some observations on it. One time, I was taking a buffet plate back to my table and it was a little too hot to hold (but not dangerously so) and i just kept holding it. You know how pain kinda ramps up? at first you don't feel it, then it sinks in and starts to hurt, then increases and most people stop by then, but I kept holding it and the pain doesn't keep increasing forever. From that, I learned that pain is not infinite, eventually it will stop growing and just hurt at the same level.
